newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU offers aid for Poland floods.
newsitem.headline: EU offers aid for Poland floods.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday it was granting more than 65 million European currency units in aid ($70 million) to help Poland recover from devastating floods.
It also said it was asking the European Investment Bank to consider loans to the region.
"We want to react quickly to a human disaster," External Affairs Commissioner Hans van den Broek said.
The floods, the worst in centuries, have put more than 5,000 sq km (2,000 sq miles) of Poland's south and west under water and killed at least 55 people.

Van den Broek told a news conference that the money, added to some 300,000 Ecus already released, would come from the European Union's PHARE programme, the funding project aimed at former Communist countries seeking EU membership.
Poland, along with the Czech republic, Hungary, Estonia and Slovenia, have been tipped by the Commission to be in a first wave of eastern European countries to be brought into the EU bloc.
Van den Broek said he had ordered Commission staff to look for PHARE funds to help the Czech Republic, also hit by floods.

At the same news conference, Commissioner Emma Bonino said her humanitarian aid office had already released 500,000 Ecus in emergency aid and had another two million at hand -- 1.4 million for Poland and 600,000 for the Czech Republic. $1 = 0.925 ecu REUTER
